info.name: Todo Application API
info.description:
# Todo Application API

A full-featured REST API for learning, teaching, and experimentation. It covers a wide range of common API patterns including authentication, resource management, real-time streaming, webhooks, and analytics.

## Feature Areas

**Authentication** — Register and log in users, manage sessions with JWT access and refresh tokens, and retrieve the current user's profile.

**Tasks** — Create and manage todo items with support for priorities, statuses, pagination, search, and sorting. Tasks can be nested (parent/child relationships) and scoped to the authenticated user.

**Posts** — Create and manage blog-style posts with categories, statuses (draft/published/archived), and slug-based lookup. Posts can be filtered, searched, and scoped to the current user.

**Comments** — Add comments to posts, list comments per post, and manage individual comments (read, update, delete). Comments can also be scoped to the authenticated user.

**Products** — Create and manage product listings with category, featured, and published filters. Products support pagination, search, and per-user scoping.

**Webhooks** — Subscribe to API events and receive HTTP callbacks. Manage subscriptions (create, update, delete, test) and inspect delivery events with retry support.

**Analytics** — Query request logs and aggregate counts across the API. Supports filtering by method, path, status code, and time range, with grouping options.

**Server-Sent Events (SSE)** — Subscribe to real-time event streams for tasks, posts, products, and comments using the SSE protocol.

## Getting Started

Set the `baseUrl` environment variable to your server's base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:3000`). Register a user, log in to receive an `accessToken`, and use it as a Bearer token for authenticated requests. The `refreshToken` can be used to obtain a new `accessToken` when it expires.

item.description: Endpoints for creating and managing todo tasks. Supports listing all tasks or only the authenticated user's tasks, creating new tasks, and performing read/update/delete operations on individual tasks by ID. Tasks support priorities, statuses, pagination, search, and sort order. Tasks can also have child tasks (subtasks) accessible via the `children` subfolder.
